examples.en: He tried to force the door open.
If you force a child, he dislikes it even more.
You should talk it out; forcing things is not okay.
I crammed all my clothes into the bag by force.

examples.ko: 회의에서 우격다짐 식으로 결정하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't make decisions in a meeting by pushing them through.
I couldn't resist the pressure and ended up going along.

explain: 말이 통하지 않을 때 힘이나 기세로 억지로 밀어붙이는 느낌이에요. 사람에게 억지로 시킬 때도, 물건을 억지로 밀어 넣을 때도 써요. '우격다짐으로 하다', '우격다짐으로 밀어붙이다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling pushed so hard that I finally gave in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우격다짐'에 '하다'를 붙여 억지로 밀어붙이는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning to force something through.

phrases.en: The company forced the plan through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대가 있는데도 억지로 진행할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is pushed through despite objections.

phrases.en: If you force a child, they come to hate studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: '억지로'는 더 쉽고 일상적인 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '억지로' is an easier, everyday word with a similar meaning.
phrases.en_equiv: to make someone do it against their will

explain_en: It carries the feel of pushing something through by force or sheer pressure when reasoning doesn't work. It is used both for forcing people and for cramming things in. People say '우격다짐으로 하다' or '우격다짐으로 밀어붙이다'.

examples.ko: 동생은 숙제를 안 하려고 잔꾀를 부려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling plays little tricks to avoid doing homework.

examples.ko: 잔꾀만 부리지 말고 열심히 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just play tricks, try to work hard.
The teacher will quickly catch on to a trick like that.

examples.ko: 잔꾀 부리다가 오히려 일이 더 늘었어요.
examples.en: I tried to cut corners and ended up with more work.

examples.ko: 저 아이는 잔꾀가 많아서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: That kid is full of petty tricks, so you have to be careful.

examples.ko: 잔꾀로 시험을 통과하려는 건 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not good to try to pass the exam with cheap tricks.

explain: '꾀'는 좋게도 나쁘게도 쓰지만, '잔꾀'는 얕고 보잘것없는 꾀라서 거의 부정적으로 써요. '잔꾀를 부리다'가 가장 흔한 짝이고, 편하려고 요령을 피우는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: If you use petty tricks, you get caught quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 꾀를 직접 쓴다는 점이 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 부리다, but makes it clear that one actually uses the trick.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 잔꾀가 많아서 힘든 일을 잘 피해요.
phrases.en: That child has lots of little tricks and avoids hard work well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말할 때 쓰고, 요령만 피운다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person, with a negative sense of dodging effort.
phrases.en_equiv: to be full of little tricks

phrases.en: I fell for my friend's trick and ended up cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 얕은 꾀에 속아서 손해 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one is fooled by another's petty trick and loses out.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall for a petty trick

explain_en: '꾀' can be good or bad, but '잔꾀' is a shallow, petty scheme and is almost always negative. '잔꾀를 부리다' is the most common pairing, with a feeling of dodging effort to take it easy.

examples.ko: 옛날에 그 나라를 정복한 왕이 있었어요.
examples.en: Long ago there was a king who conquered that country.
His dream is to conquer Mount Everest.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 드디어 이 지역 시장을 정복했어요.
examples.en: Our team finally conquered the market in this region.
I study every day to conquer the difficult exam.

examples.ko: 그 왕은 넓은 땅을 정복하고 큰 제국을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The king conquered vast lands and built a great empire.

examples.ko: 이 게임의 마지막 단계를 정복하기가 정말 어려워요.
examples.en: It is really hard to conquer the last stage of this game.

explain: 힘으로 땅이나 나라를 차지할 때도 쓰고, 산이나 어려운 시험을 끝까지 해냈다는 비유로도 많이 써요. '이기다'는 경기나 싸움의 결과에 쓰고, '정복하다'는 대상을 완전히 내 것으로 만든다는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 오랜 전쟁 끝에 정복됐어요.
phrases.en: That country was conquered after a long war.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정복하다'의 피동형으로, 차지당하는 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form speaks from the side of the one being conquered.

phrases.example: 그 팀이 높은 산 정복에 성공했어요.
phrases.en: The team succeeded in conquering the high mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '정복'을 써서 끝까지 해냈다는 뜻을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form stresses that they achieved it in the end.

phrases.en: Alexander is a famous conqueror.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정복하다'에 '-자'를 붙여 정복한 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-자' to the word gives the person who conquers.

explain_en: Overcome a mountain, land or challenge completely. It is used for taking over land or a country by force, and also figuratively for mastering a mountain or a hard exam. '이기다' is about the result of a match or fight, while '정복하다' carries the feeling of making the target completely yours.

t90.ax: His dream is to conquer Mount Everest.

examples.en: The child eats while dribbling soup.
The pants are long and drag on the floor.
Water is leaking out of the plastic bag.

examples.ko: 그 일을 질질 끌다가 결국 늦었어요.
examples.en: I dragged that task out and ended up late.
The puppy trails its leash around.
I watched the movie with tears streaming down.

explain: 액체가 계속 흐르거나 물건이 바닥에 끌릴 때 쓰는 흉내말이에요. 일을 빨리 끝내지 않고 시간을 끄는 것도 '질질 끌다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Please don't drag the meeting out too long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 빨리 끝내지 않고 시간을 끄는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means dragging out time instead of finishing quickly.

phrases.en: The long skirt drags on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 끝이 바닥에 닿아 끌릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the end of something touches and drags along the floor.

phrases.en: I ate the ice cream while dripping it all over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 액체를 계속 흘릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when liquid keeps dripping.

explain_en: It imitates liquid dribbling steadily or something dragging along the ground. Putting off finishing something is also 질질 끌다.

en: to flounder; to writhe; to struggle

examples.en: A child who fell in the water is flailing about.
I cannot swim, so I floundered in the water.
I struggled through the snow and barely got home.
There are many people around me struggling under debt.

examples.ko: 잠에서 덜 깬 채로 허우적거려서 컵을 쏟았어요.
examples.en: I was still half asleep and flailed around, so I spilled the cup.

examples.ko: 일에 파묻혀 허우적거리다 보니 한 달이 갔어요.
examples.en: I was buried in work, struggling, and a month went by.

explain: 물이나 진흙 속에서 팔다리를 마구 휘젓는 모습이 기본이고, '빚에·일에 허우적거리다'처럼 힘든 상황에서 헤어 나오지 못하는 모습에도 비유로 써요. '허우적대다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The child is flailing about in the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허우적거리다'와 뜻이 같고 조금 더 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'heoujeokgeorida' and a bit shorter.

phrases.example: 그는 허우적거리며 겨우 물 밖으로 나왔어요.
phrases.en: He floundered and barely made it out of the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동작이 이어지는 모습을 문장 안에서 연결할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect the ongoing action within a sentence.

phrases.en: These days I'm struggling under a pile of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 상황에서 헤어 나오지 못하는 모습을 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for being stuck in a hard situation.

explain_en: The basic image is thrashing arms and legs in water or mud, and it is also used figuratively, as in '빚에/일에 허우적거리다', for being stuck in a hard situation. It means the same as '허우적대다', so you can swap them.

examples.ko: 경찰의 회유에도 그는 입을 열지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even with the police coaxing him, he didn't open his mouth.
You shouldn't fall for sweet-talking persuasion.

examples.ko: 회유와 협박을 번갈아 쓰는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people alternate between coaxing and threatening.
His attempt to win people over didn't work.

examples.ko: 부모님의 회유 끝에 결국 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: After much coaxing from my parents, I finally went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 회유가 안 통하자 그는 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: When coaxing didn't work, he got angry.

explain: '달래다'는 따뜻한 느낌이지만 '회유'는 좋은 조건이나 말로 상대를 내 쪽으로 돌려놓으려는 의도가 있어요. 그래서 '회유와 협박'처럼 다소 부정적인 문맥에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: He told the truth despite coaxing and threats.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 말과 겁주기를 함께 말할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for sweet talk combined with threats.

phrases.en: I was talked around by my friend and changed the plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 설득에 마음이 바뀔 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for being won over by someone's persuasion.

phrases.en: The company tried to win the employees over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '회유'의 동사형으로, 사람을 달래서 내 편으로 만들려 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, for trying to bring people to your side.

explain_en: '달래다' feels warm, but '회유' carries an intention to bring someone over to your side with good terms or words. So it often appears in somewhat negative contexts like '회유와 협박' (coaxing and threats).

examples.en: After standing and working all day, I'm going to wreck my body.

examples.ko: 젊을 때 무리하면 나이 들어 골병들어요.
examples.en: If you overwork when you are young, your body breaks down when you get old.

examples.ko: 아버지는 오랫동안 힘든 일을 하다가 골병드셨어요.
examples.en: My father did hard work for a long time and ended up with chronic ailments.
I nearly ruined my body carrying the moving boxes alone.

examples.ko: 야근이 계속되면 몸이 골병들 수 있어요.
examples.en: If overtime goes on, your body can get seriously worn down.
If you don't rest early, you'll break down, so be careful.

explain: 겉으로는 잘 안 보이지만 오랫동안 쌓인 피로나 무리 때문에 몸속이 상하는 것을 말해요. '골병이 들다'로도 쓰고, 주로 몸이 상한 것에 써요. 어간이 'ㄹ'로 끝나서 '골병드니까', '골병드셨어요'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져요.

phrases.example: 무거운 짐을 매일 들면 허리에 골병이 들어요.
phrases.en: If you carry heavy loads every day, your back gets worn out for good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골병들다'를 조사와 함께 풀어 쓴 꼴이고 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the spaced-out form of 골병들다 with a particle and means the same.

phrases.en: Take breaks while you work so you don't wear out your body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라고 조언할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting phrase used when advising someone to be careful.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to ruin your health

phrases.en: If you overdo it, your body gets damaged.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골병들다'보다 쉽고 뜻이 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler and broader expression than 골병들다.
phrases.en_equiv: for one's body to be damaged

explain_en: It means your body is damaged inside from long-built-up fatigue or overwork, even if it doesn't show outside. It is also said as '골병이 들다' and is mostly used for physical damage. The stem ends in 'ㄹ', so the ㄹ drops: '골병드니까', '골병드셨어요'.

examples.en: The doctor picked up the scalpel and began the surgery.
A scalpel is very sharp, so you have to be careful.
The scalpels are laid out cleanly in the operating room.
The nurse handed the doctor a scalpel.
The students dissected a frog with a scalpel.
With just one scalpel, he finished a hard operation.

explain: 수술할 때 쓰는 작은 칼이에요. 일상에서는 '수술용 칼'이라고도 해요. '메스를 가하다'는 문제를 고치려고 과감하게 손댄다는 비유로도 쓰여요.

phrases.en: We have to take a scalpel to the outdated system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 고치려고 과감하게 손댄다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Figurative: to take bold action to fix a problem.

explain_en: A small knife used in surgery, also called 수술용 칼. The phrase 메스를 가하다 is used figuratively for taking bold action to fix a problem.

examples.en: The doctor stitched up the deep wound right away.

examples.ko: 다친 부위를 봉합한 뒤에 주사를 맞았어요.
examples.en: After the injured area was stitched, I got a shot.

examples.ko: 정부가 갈등을 봉합하려고 계속 노력하고 있어요.
examples.en: The government keeps trying to patch up the conflict.
Even after the wound is stitched, you have to be careful for a few days.

examples.ko: 싸움을 대충 봉합했지만 마음은 풀리지 않았어요.
examples.en: We patched up the fight roughly, but our feelings were not settled.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 갈등을 봉합하고 다시 손을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The two companies settled their conflict and joined hands again.

explain: 목적어로 '상처'나 '갈등'이 자주 와요. 갈등을 봉합한다고 하면 뿌리부터 풀었다기보다 일단 수습했다는 느낌이에요. 일상에서 옷이나 천은 '꿰매다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 오해를 풀고 갈등을 봉합했어요.
phrases.en: The two cleared up the misunderstanding and patched up their conflict.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈등을 일단 수습한다는 비유적인 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use: getting a conflict under control for now.

phrases.en: The wound is deep, so it needs to be stitched right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사가 꼭 해야 할 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something a doctor must do.

phrases.en: I sewed up the torn pants with a needle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 천에는 '봉합하다' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 봉합하다 for clothes and fabric.

explain_en: Its object is often '상처' (wound) or '갈등' (conflict). Saying you 봉합 a conflict suggests it was settled for now rather than solved at the root. For clothes or cloth in daily life, say '꿰매다'.

t90.ax: The doctor stitched up the deep wound right away.

en: to perform a medical procedure; to perform surgery

examples.en: The doctor performed the procedure personally.
This clinic does the treatment with lasers.
It takes about thirty minutes to do the procedure.
How will you treat this area?
The spot treated yesterday still hurts.
It is safer when a specialist does the procedure.

explain: '시술하다'는 치료하는 사람이 주어예요. 받는 사람은 '시술을 받다'라고 해요. 큰 치료는 '수술하다', 가볍게 몸에 하는 치료는 '시술하다'를 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The director performs the procedure personally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 사람을 높이는 말이에요. 병원에서 직원이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Honors the person receiving it. Hospital staff often use it.

phrases.en: It didn't hurt during the procedure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료가 진행되는 시간을 말할 때 써요. '-는 동안'을 붙이면 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time while the treatment is going on. Just add -는 동안.

phrases.en: We don't perform a procedure for small wounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료를 하지 않는다는 부정형이에요. 의사가 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning no procedure is done. Used when a doctor explains.

explain_en: The subject of 시술하다 is the person giving the treatment; the patient says '시술을 받다' instead. For major operations Koreans say 수술하다, and for lighter treatments on the body they often use 시술하다.

examples.en: I press my shoulders firmly with my fingers.
My neck was stiff, so I pressed on it myself.
Mom pressed on my back for me.
They say pressing on this spot is good for digestion.
I learned how to press on the soles of the feet.
Please don't press too hard.

explain: 몸의 한 곳을 손가락이나 손바닥으로 꾹 눌러서 풀어 주는 것을 말해요. 일상에서는 '지압을 하다'나 '꾹꾹 누르다'라고도 해요. '어깨를 지압하다'처럼 누르는 부분 뒤에 '를'을 써요.

phrases.en: I gave my mom's shoulders an acupressure massage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 위해 해 줄 때 써요. 윗사람에게는 '드리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doing it for someone else; use 'deurida' for elders.

phrases.en: I press the sore spot firmly with my fingers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지압하다'를 쉬운 말로 바꿔 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say 'jiaphada'.

phrases.en: It feels refreshing when I press the soles of my feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지압의 효과를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common connected form for describing the effect of acupressure.

explain_en: It means pressing firmly on one part of the body with fingers or palms to loosen it up. In daily talk people also say '지압을 하다' or '꾹꾹 누르다'. The pressed body part takes '를', as in '어깨를 지압하다'.

examples.ko: 배가 기울자 승객들이 서둘러 구명정에 올라탔어요.
examples.en: When the ship tilted, the passengers hurriedly climbed into the lifeboat.

examples.ko: 구명정은 배에 탄 사람 수에 맞게 준비해 둬야 해요.
examples.en: Lifeboats have to be prepared to match the number of people on board.

examples.ko: 바다 위에서 구명정을 타고 이틀을 버텼어요.
examples.en: They survived two days on the sea in a lifeboat.
There weren't enough lifeboats, so everyone was anxious.

examples.ko: 구조대가 멀리 떠 있는 구명정으로 다가갔어요.
examples.en: The rescue team approached the lifeboat floating far away.

examples.ko: 승무원이 구명정 내리는 방법을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: A crew member showed us how to lower the lifeboat.

explain: '구명보트'라고도 말하고, 사람이 입는 것은 '구명조끼'예요. 배 사고 뉴스나 안전 교육에서 들을 수 있는 말이에요. 보통 '구명정에 타다', '구명정을 내리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The passengers boarded the lifeboat one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구명정'과 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서는 이 말을 더 쉽게 알아들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the same as 구명정 and is easier to understand in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The sailors lowered the lifeboat into the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배 사고에서 구명정을 물에 띄우는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes putting the lifeboat into the water during a ship emergency.

phrases.en: I put on a life jacket and got into the lifeboat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구명정과 함께 알아 두면 좋은 말이에요. 사람이 입는 안전 장비예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Worth learning with 구명정. It is the safety gear a person wears.

explain_en: It is also called '구명보트', and the thing a person wears is a '구명조끼' (life jacket). You hear it in news about ship accidents and in safety training. Typical patterns are '구명정에 타다' and '구명정을 내리다'.

examples.ko: 사우나에서 뜨거운 탕 다음에 냉탕에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: At the sauna I got into the cold bath after the hot one.

examples.ko: 냉탕 물이 너무 차가워서 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: The cold bath was so cold that I screamed.
The kids played happily in the cold bath.
Going back and forth between the cold and hot baths feels refreshing.
Take a shower before you get into the cold bath.
The cold bath was like ice, so I got out quickly.

explain: 대중목욕탕에서 찬물이 담긴 탕이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '온탕'이고, 이 둘을 같이 써서 비유하는 말도 있어요.

phrases.en: to swing between hot and cold
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황이나 분위기가 좋았다 나빴다 자주 바뀔 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to say conditions or moods keep changing between good and bad.

explain_en: It is the bath filled with cold water at a public bathhouse. Its pair is '온탕' (hot bath), and the two are also used together in a figurative expression.

examples.en: Is there a nonstop bus to Seoul?

examples.ko: 직행으로 가면 두 시간밖에 안 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take the express, it takes only two hours.
After work I went straight home.

examples.ko: 직행 열차는 표가 조금 더 비싸요.
examples.en: The express train ticket is a bit more expensive.
A direct shuttle runs from the airport to the hotel.

examples.ko: 이 버스는 직행이라서 중간에 안 서요.
examples.en: This bus is nonstop, so it doesn't stop on the way.

explain: 직행은 중간에 서지 않고 곧장 가는 거예요. 모든 정류장에 서는 버스는 '완행'이라고 하고, 시외버스에서 '직행'과 '완행'을 구분해서 불러요. 멈추지 않고 바로 간다는 뜻으로 '직행하다'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I took the express bus to Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중간에 서지 않고 가는 버스를 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for a bus that does not stop along the way.

phrases.example: 이 직행 열차는 중간에 서지 않아요.
phrases.en: This express train doesn't stop along the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스뿐 아니라 기차에도 직행을 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use 직행 with trains as well as buses.

phrases.en: This bus goes straight to the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 '곧장 간다'는 움직임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb, it describes the action of going straight there.

explain_en: Going straight to destination without stopping or detour. 직행 is going straight to the destination without stopping on the way. A bus that stops at every stop is 완행, and intercity buses are labeled either 직행 or 완행. It is also used as a verb, 직행하다, for heading somewhere directly.

examples.ko: 고속도로에서는 추월 차선을 잘 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: On the highway, you have to follow the passing-lane rules well.

examples.ko: 이 구간은 추월 금지라서 천천히 가야 해요.
examples.en: Passing is prohibited in this section, so we have to go slowly.

examples.ko: 무리한 추월은 사고로 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Reckless passing can lead to an accident.

examples.ko: 뒤차의 추월을 막으려고 속도를 올리면 위험해요.
examples.en: It's dangerous to speed up to stop the car behind from passing.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 마지막 바퀴에서 추월에 성공했어요.
examples.en: Our team succeeded in overtaking on the last lap.
It's a narrow road where passing is impossible.

explain: 앞에 가는 차나 사람을 앞질러 갈 때 쓰고, 도로 표지판의 '추월 금지'로 많이 봐요. 일상 대화에서는 '앞지르기'라고도 해요. 매출이나 순위를 앞선다는 뜻으로 '추월하다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The car behind me passed me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '추월'에 '-하다'를 붙인 동사로, 앞에 가는 것을 앞지른다는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 추월, describing the action of getting ahead of something in front.

phrases.en: You have to be careful when overtaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추월'과 같은 뜻의 순우리말이라 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word with the same meaning as 추월, more comfortable in daily talk.

phrases.example: 이 도로는 추월 사고가 자주 나요.
phrases.en: Overtaking accidents happen often on this road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추월하다가 생긴 교통사고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for traffic accidents that happen while overtaking.

explain_en: It is used when you go ahead of a car or person in front, and you often see it on road signs as '추월 금지' (no passing). In daily talk it is also called '앞지르기'. The verb '추월하다' is also used for surpassing sales or rankings.
